intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1), also called cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the keratin-1 gene (KRT1; 139350) on chromosome 12q13.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is also called cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Abstract does not use the term 'cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis' (abstract only).

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the keratin-1 gene (KRT1).
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes
checks.explanation: The paper names mutations in both keratin 1 and keratin 10. It does not specify heterozygosity or single out KRT1 for an AEI1 subtype.

checks.claim: The KRT1 gene is located on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes
checks.explanation: The paper names the keratin 1 gene. The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates it.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a clinical variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma), a keratinopathic ichthyosis. Affected individuals have blistering and erythroderma in early life. Later they develop episodes of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques, mainly on the trunk and proximal limbs, which flare and then fade. Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis may be present. Skin biopsy shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a clinical variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma).
checks.evidence_quote: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis (AEI) is a rare phenotypic variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis (EI), also known as congenital bullous ichthyosiform erythroderma
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Epidermolytic ichthyosis is a keratinopathic ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Abstract does not describe it as keratinopathic or mention keratins.

checks.claim: Individuals with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis have blistering and erythroderma in early life.
checks.evidence_quote: A 30-year-old white woman developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months.
checks.explanation: Blistering in infancy described; erythroderma not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: Individuals with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis later develop episodes of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques, mainly on the trunk and proximal limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: Characteristically, they also develop recurrent outbreaks of annular, polycyclic, erythematous, and scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The annular and polycyclic scaly plaques in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis flare and then fade.
checks.evidence_quote: that were pruritic, enlarged slowly, and then resolved
checks.explanation: Plaques enlarged and then resolved.

checks.claim: Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis may be present in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by erythematous, polycyclic, and migratory scaly plaques accompanied by palmoplantar keratoderma
checks.explanation: Palmoplantar keratoderma is described, and the table shows it is present in some cases only.

checks.claim: Skin biopsy in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic examination of these annular plaques revealed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Sahn et al. (1992) described annular epidermolytic ichthyosis as a distinct phenotype. Patients had bullous erythroderma in infancy. Later they had recurrent annular, polycyclic, erythematous scaly plaques on the trunk and extremities, which came and went over weeks to months. Histology showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

checks.claim: Sahn et al. (1992) described annular epidermolytic ichthyosis as a distinct phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: This kindred may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: Title 'a unique phenotype' and conclusion support this.

checks.claim: Patients with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis described by Sahn et al. (1992) had bullous erythroderma in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: A 30-year-old white woman developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months.
checks.explanation: Bullous lesions in infancy described for the proband; 'erythroderma' not stated, and the children's course is only summarized as bullous ichthyosis.

checks.claim: Patients with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis described by Sahn et al. (1992) later had recurrent annular, polycyclic, erythematous scaly plaques on the trunk and extremities.
checks.evidence_quote: At the age of 27 years, she developed numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities that were pruritic, enlarged slowly, and then resolved.
checks.explanation: Plaques described in the proband, but recurrence is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The plaques in the patients described by Sahn et al. (1992) came and went over weeks to months.
checks.explanation: Abstract says plaques enlarged slowly and resolved but gives no timescale of weeks to months.

checks.claim: Histology in the patients with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis described by Sahn et al. (1992) showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic examination of these annular plaques revealed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Sybert et al. (1999) studied families with a similar episodic phenotype, which they called cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. Affected individuals had epidermolytic hyperkeratosis together with intermittent flares of polycyclic erythematous scaly plaques. Some also had palmoplantar keratoderma.

checks.claim: Sybert et al. (1999) studied families with an episodic phenotype similar to annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, which they called cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.evidence_quote: 11 (mother of case 10) | 18 years/F | Intermittent and migratory erythematous plaques.
checks.explanation: Sybert et al. (1999) is listed as reporting one family with AEI. The paper never gives the name 'cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis' and does not mention more than one family.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the families studied by Sybert et al. (1999) had epidermolytic hyperkeratosis together with intermittent flares of polycyclic erythematous scaly plaques.
checks.evidence_quote: At 3 years of age, migratory and intermittent, hyperkeratotic, erythematous plaques on the chest, back, and flexures.
checks.explanation: The paper describes intermittent erythematous plaques for the Sybert cases. It does not mention 'polycyclic' or epidermolytic hyperkeratosis for those cases.

checks.claim: Some affected individuals in the families studied by Sybert et al. (1999) had palmoplantar keratoderma.
checks.evidence_quote: Intermittent palmoplantar hyperkeratosis. Intermittent episodes of erythroderma and palmoplantar keratoderma.
checks.explanation: Palmoplantar involvement is reported for the Sybert cases.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis follows an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance, consistent with the heterozygous keratin mutations found in affected families (Sybert et al., 1999).

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis follows an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes
checks.explanation: The paper describes the cause as dominant mutations, and EI is described as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Sybert et al. (1999) found heterozygous keratin mutations in families affected by annular epidermolytic ichthyosis (cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Concerns Sybert et al. (1999); no mutations reported in this abstract.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is genetically heterogeneous. Mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10) has also been reported in this phenotype (Joh et al., 1997). That form is designated AEI2.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports only a KRT10 mutation and does not discuss genetic heterogeneity or other genes.

checks.claim: Joh et al. (1997) reported mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10) in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals, resulting in an arginine to glutamate substitution at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment.
checks.explanation: A KRT10 mutation in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is reported.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis caused by KRT10 mutation is designated AEI2.
checks.explanation: The AEI2 designation is OMIM nomenclature and is not in the paper.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of families with cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, Sybert et al. (1999) found heterozygous mutations in the 2B domain of keratin-1 (KRT1). The more severe classic epidermolytic ichthyosis is usually caused by mutations in the highly conserved helix boundary motifs. Sybert et al. (1999) proposed that mutations in the 2B domain lead to this milder, episodic phenotype.

checks.claim: Sybert et al. (1999) found heterozygous mutations in the 2B domain of keratin-1 (KRT1) in affected members of families with cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Concerns Sybert et al. (1999); not in this paper.

checks.claim: Classic epidermolytic ichthyosis, which is more severe than cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, is usually caused by mutations in the highly conserved helix boundary motifs of keratins.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. No molecular data in this abstract.

checks.claim: Sybert et al. (1999) proposed that mutations in the 2B domain of keratin-1 lead to the milder, episodic phenotype of cyclic ichthyosis with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. Concerns Sybert et al. (1999); not in this paper.

Lesions on trunk and proximal extremities
